# Lab 18.4: Row-Level Security

## What We Are Going to Do
Create row access policies so each user sees only the rows for their region, and check that the filter is applied.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create two policies.** Replace `YOUR_EMAIL` and `YOUR_PROJECT`.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE ROW ACCESS POLICY india_only
ON lab18_private.users
GRANT TO ('serviceAccount:bq-analyst@YOUR_PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com')
FILTER USING (country = 'India');

CREATE OR REPLACE ROW ACCESS POLICY admins_all
ON lab18_private.users
GRANT TO ('user:YOUR_EMAIL')
FILTER USING (TRUE);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[CLI] Compare results.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'SELECT country, COUNT(*) FROM lab18_private.users GROUP BY country ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5'

gcloud config set auth/impersonate_service_account $ANALYST

gcloud config unset auth/impersonate_service_account</span>

   You see every country. The analyst sees only India.

3. **[SQL] A mapping-table pattern.** Map users to regions in a table instead of one policy per user:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab18.user_region (email STRING, country STRING);
INSERT INTO lab18.user_region VALUES ('YOUR_EMAIL', 'Japan');

CREATE OR REPLACE ROW ACCESS POLICY by_mapping
ON lab18_private.users
GRANT TO ('allAuthenticatedUsers')
FILTER USING (country IN (SELECT country FROM lab18.user_region WHERE email = SESSION_USER()));</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] See the policies.** Open `lab18_private.users → Details → Row access policies`.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Policy | Filter applied automatically |
| No matching policy | User sees no rows |
| `SESSION_USER()` | Dynamic, table-driven filtering |
| Users | Never see the filter itself |
